neighbours.label: the word right after a risk/likelihood predicate ('more prone to', 'more likely to', 'at high risk of', 'common site for')
fire: Older dogs are more prone to joint problems than young ones.
Smokers are far more likely to develop lung disease.
People with diabetes are at higher risk of foot infections.
Children who skip breakfast are more likely to feel tired at school.
The knee is a common site for sports injuries in teenagers.
Night shift workers are more susceptible to sleep disorders.
Travellers in the region face a high risk of catching malaria.
Thin-skinned fruit is especially vulnerable to frost damage.
quiet: Older dogs are often calmer and gentler than young ones.
Smokers are often told about free help to quit.
People with diabetes are encouraged to check their feet daily.
Children who eat breakfast are able to focus better at school.
The knee is a joint that connects the thigh and the shin.
Night shift workers are paid a little more per hour.
Travellers in the region can visit several old temples.
Thin-skinned fruit is usually picked early in the morning.

notes: card: 'prone to', 'more likely to feel', 'common site for', 'high risk of encountering', 'have more food allergies'. Quiet keeps health topics with ability/neutral predicates.
